title: How to book a Dooars safari: Jaldapara, Gorumara and more
summary: Dooars safaris are run by the West Bengal forest department and sold per jeep, online when booking is open and at counters in Lataguri and Madarihat for any slots left. Book as early as you can for November to March, share a jeep to cut costs, and remember that every park closes from 16 June to 15 September.
meta_description: Book Jaldapara, Gorumara, Chilapata and Buxa safaris: how slots work, online and counter booking, indicative 2025–26 costs, elephant rides and closure dates.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: All safaris in the Dooars parks are run by the West Bengal forest department. You do not book them through a private operator in the way you might at some parks elsewhere in India. Instead the department sells a fixed number of jeep slots for each route and each time of day, and every jeep carries a driver and a forest guide.

In recent seasons the department has sold many of these slots online a few weeks ahead, through its official booking pages and those of the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation (WBFDC). Whatever is not sold online is usually sold at the counters, at Lataguri for Gorumara and at Madarihat for Jaldapara, often from the afternoon before. Guests in WBFDC lodges can sometimes book at the lodge reception.

The rules have changed more than once in the last few years: which slots go online, how far ahead they open, what ID you need and what the fees are. Treat everything in this guide as indicative, and check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: When the parks are open
paras: Every national park and wildlife sanctuary in North Bengal, including Jaldapara, Gorumara, Chapramari, Neora Valley and the tourism zones of Buxa Tiger Reserve, closes for the monsoon from 16 June to 15 September. This is for the animals' breeding season and because heavy rain washes out forest tracks and bridges. Tea-garden villages such as Samsing remain open, but there are no safaris.

The parks reopen on 16 September, but some routes open later if the tracks need repair. October brings the Durga Puja holidays, when the whole of Bengal seems to travel and slots sell out quickly. The grass is still tall then, which can hide rhinos. From December to April the grass is shorter, the forest is drier and sightings are better.

Parks can also close at short notice for a day or two, for official animal counts, elections, security reasons or after a forest fire. A good lodge will tell you, but it is worth looking at local news the week you travel.

Busiest weeks: Durga Puja, Christmas and New Year
Closed: 16 June to 15 September every year
First slot each day: around sunrise, about 6 am in winter

sections.heading: How the safaris differ from park to park
paras: Jaldapara is about 216 km² of grassland and riverine forest on the Torsa river. Its jeep safaris drive through the grassland on set routes, and the guide looks for rhinos in the open. This is the best park in West Bengal for the one-horned rhinoceros. Most travellers stay at Madarihat, a few minutes from the gate.

Gorumara, near Lataguri, is smaller at about 80 km². Most of its trips are watchtower safaris: the jeep drives into the forest to a particular tower, you climb up, and you wait quietly while animals come to a salt lick or water body. Jatraprasad is the most popular tower. Medla includes a short bullock-cart ride and a dance by Adivasi performers at the camp. Chandrachur is quieter, and Chukchuki is mainly for birds. Nearby Chapramari Wildlife Sanctuary has its own watchtower trip.

Chilapata, near Hasimara, is dense forest with a jeep route to the ruins of Nal Raja Garh. Sightings are harder but the forest feels wilder and vehicles are few. Buxa Tiger Reserve offers jungle drives from Rajabhatkhawa, but most visitors come to walk to Buxa Fort and visit Jayanti rather than for a classic safari.

sections.heading: What it costs
paras: Safaris are priced per vehicle, not per person. Each open jeep, usually a Maruti Gypsy or similar, takes up to six passengers. The total includes the vehicle, the driver and the forest guide, plus park entry fees per person. Foreign nationals pay higher entry fees. Some parks charge a separate camera fee for larger cameras.

Because the fee is per jeep, couples and solo travellers save a great deal by sharing with others. Lodges in Lataguri and Madarihat often put guests together, and you can ask at the counter if anyone is looking to share. sections.heading: How to book, step by step
paras: Start planning four to six weeks ahead for any trip between November and March, and further ahead for Puja, Christmas and New Year. Decide which park and which slot you want: the first morning slot is best for animals and birds; the last afternoon slot gives warm light for photographs.

When online booking is open, use only the official West Bengal forest department or WBFDC booking pages. You will usually need the name, age, gender and an ID number for every passenger, and the same ID must be carried on the day. Payment is online. Keep the confirmation on your phone and on paper.

If online slots are sold out, or online booking is not open for that park, go to the counter. At Lataguri the forest department counter is in the town, near the nature interpretation centre, and at Madarihat it is near the tourist lodge and park gate. Counters usually sell the next day's remaining slots from the afternoon, and queues can start early in peak season. If you are staying in a WBFDC lodge such as Murti Banani, ask reception first; guests can often book there.

sections.heading: Elephant safaris: what to expect
paras: For many years an elephant ride at Jaldapara was the classic Dooars experience. Trained forest department elephants carried a few visitors into the tall grass near the Hollong lodge, where rhinos let an elephant come closer than a jeep. The rides have been suspended and restarted more than once since then, and the wooden Hollong lodge itself was destroyed by fire in June 2024.

For the 2025–26 season the forest department announced elephant safaris again from September, starting in the Hollong area, with only a small number of seats sold online. There is no reliable way to buy them through private agents. Some travellers choose not to ride elephants for welfare reasons. A jeep safari covers the same grassland and is much easier to book, so plan your trip around jeep safaris and treat an elephant ride as a possible extra. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: On the day: getting the most from a safari
paras: Dress in dull greens, browns or greys. Bright colours and white stand out. From November to February, dawn in an open jeep is cold, around 8–12°C, so wear layers, a hat and gloves. By late morning it is warm.

Keep your voice low, switch your phone to silent and never stand up or get out of the jeep unless the guide says so. Do not ask the driver to chase animals or go off the track; it is against the rules and stresses the animals. On watchtowers, stay still and let animals come to you. Binoculars make a big difference, as rhinos and elephants are often seen at a distance.
Tip the guide and driver if they have done a good job; ₹100–200 each per safari is usual. Take all litter back with you. Plastic is banned inside the parks.

sections.heading: If you cannot get a slot
paras: Do not give up on the trip. In Gorumara, try a different watchtower or the nearby Chapramari trip. Ask at the counter the afternoon before; cancellations do come up. At Jaldapara, try the counter early in the morning for the afternoon slot.

There is also plenty to do outside the parks. Walk on the Murti riverbed at dusk, visit the Jalpesh temple, spend a morning in the tea gardens, or go to Totopara or Chilapata. Some of the best wildlife moments in the Dooars happen on public roads at dusk, when elephants cross from one forest to another, though you should watch them from a safe distance in your vehicle.

faqs.q: Can I book a Jaldapara safari online?
faqs.a: When the forest department opens online booking, yes, through its official booking pages and those of the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation. Slots usually open some weeks ahead and sell out first for peak dates. Any slots left go on sale at the Madarihat counter. Rules and timings have changed in recent seasons. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book a Dooars safari?
faqs.a: Four to six weeks ahead for November to March, and as soon as booking opens for the Durga Puja holidays, Christmas and New Year. Midweek outside those times you may find slots a day or two ahead at the counter, but do not rely on it if the safari is the main reason for your trip.

faqs.q: Is a Gorumara safari per person or per jeep?
faqs.a: Per jeep, for up to six passengers, with park entry added per person. A full jeep costs roughly ₹2,500–3,500 for a standard watchtower trip and a little more for Medla. If you are two people, share a jeep with others to cut the cost. Fees are indicative and set by the forest department.

Jatraprasad is usually the best for rhinos and gaur and the first to sell out. Medla is the most enjoyable for families because of the bullock cart and the dance. Chandrachur is quieter and Chukchuki is mainly for birds. If you can, do two different towers on two slots.

faqs.q: Are elephant safaris running at Jaldapara?
faqs.a: They were announced again for the 2025–26 season, starting in the Hollong area, with very few seats sold online. They have been stopped and restarted several times before, so plan your trip around jeep safaris. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What ID do I need for a Dooars safari?
faqs.a: Indians usually need Aadhaar, a voter ID, a passport or a driving licence, and foreign nationals need a passport. You need ID details for every passenger when booking, and the same ID must be carried on the day. Children's ages are usually required. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Are the parks open in the monsoon?
faqs.a: No. Jaldapara, Gorumara, Chapramari, Neora Valley and the tourism zones of Buxa close every year from 16 June to 15 September. Some routes reopen later than 16 September if tracks are damaged. Tea-garden villages and towns remain open, but there are no safaris.

Yes. Foreign nationals book in the same way, with passport details, but pay higher entry fees. No special permit is needed for the Dooars. If you are continuing to Bhutan, arrange your Bhutan visa and tour in advance.

faqs.q: What is the best time of day for a Dooars safari?
faqs.a: The first slot of the morning, around sunrise, is usually best: animals are active, the air is cool and birds are calling. The last afternoon slot is second best, with warm light for photographs. Mid-day slots are hotter and quieter, especially from March onwards.
